vulnerability_analysis: The reentrancy vulnerability exists in swapAndSendDividends() which calls external contracts via low-level calls without updating buyAmount/sellAmount state variables first. During the external call to dividendTracker or marketing/dev wallets, we can re-enter the contract through a fallback function that calls transfer again. Since buyAmount and sellAmount aren't updated until after the external calls, we can drain funds multiple times.
attack_strategy: Create a malicious contract that receives ETH from the dividend distribution and re-enters the EthBurn contract by calling transfer again. This will trigger swapAndSendDividends multiple times before buyAmount/sellAmount are reset to zero.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Deploy a malicious contract that can receive ETH and re-enter EthBurn. 2. Ensure the EthBurn contract has accumulated fees (buyAmount/sellAmount > 0). 3. Trigger a transfer that causes swapAndSendDividends to execute. 4. During the ETH transfer to our malicious contract, re-enter EthBurn by calling transfer again. 5. Exploit the un-updated buyAmount/sellAmount to drain funds multiple times.
